news.title: Notion’s Confusing Credit Model
news.gist: Notion now gives each Business and Enterprise seat two separate AI credit balances, split by whether Notion or the user picks the model, and Litterst argues the split hands customers complexity that Notion should absorb itself.
points: Neither balance can be pooled or shared, and running dry on one pauses that kind of work even when the other still has credits
A third, shared workspace balance can top up either pool, which Litterst says undercuts the reason for having two
He traces Notion’s AI pricing from a flat add-on to bundling, then metered credits, and now the split wallets
His simpler fix: give Custom Agents their own balance so people who never use them can ignore those credits
nums: Standard credits per Business member each month, used when Notion picks the model
Select credits per Business member each month, used when the member picks the model or runs Custom Agents
$10 per 1,000 credits
price of the simpler credit model Notion launched with Custom Agents
changes in the issue’s weekly roundup
news.why: If you buy Notion Business or Enterprise, check which of the two credit pools your team’s AI work draws on, because an empty pool stops that work even while the other still has credits.

news.title: HubSpot cuts Free plan email sends from 2,000 to 300 a month in a 314-change week
news.gist: PricingSaaS’s review of 19–25 Oct describes a busy week, well above the recent average, led by HubSpot’s smaller free email allowance, with increases outnumbering cuts and promotions running above their norm.
points: Vercel and Acquia cut usage quotas, and Acquia also turned its top uptime SLA into a paid add-on
Krea’s removal of Nodes Agent from Pro and Max flipped back and forth, and fal’s video cut is flagged as a test arm
Tray, Stedi and Trust & Will put prices on the page that used to be hidden or behind contact sales
Intercom’s new-customer discount on annual Essential came back, bringing the $29 list seat down to $19

news.why: A week this busy means a plan you priced last month may have changed, so check limits and add-ons as well as the list price before renewing.

news.title: HubSpot cuts Free plan email sends from 2,000 to 300, shifts Starter onto shared Credits
news.gist: HubSpot shrank the Free plan’s email allowance and moved Starter’s email sending from a cap tied to contact tier onto its shared Credits pool, which the article reads as giving HubSpot one lever for tuning email limits later.
points: On Starter, email now competes for the same credit budget as other credit-spending actions
The article suggests watching whether other Starter features with fixed caps move onto Credits next
It is the latest in a run of HubSpot changes that recently included Starter automation and pipeline limits

35 days

news.why: Starter customers can’t compare the new email allowance with the old cap until they know how many Credits a send uses, so ask HubSpot before planning a campaign calendar.

news.title: Baseten cuts Reflection Beam rates up to 72% four days after launch
news.gist: Baseten cut input, cached-input and output token prices for its newly listed Reflection Beam model within days of adding it, and PricingSaaS argues launch-day rates are no floor for buyers of hosted models.
points: Reflection Beam was added to Baseten’s Model APIs catalog alongside Meta Muse Spark Open at the prices now being cut
The article ties it to an earlier Baseten move that cut DeepSeek V4.1 Flash’s cached-input price soon after listing
It suggests watching whether the lower rates hold, given how often Baseten has repriced since July

news.title: Developer Tool Pricing Changes: October 19–25, 2026
news.gist: AgentDeals’ digest for our week is mostly model retirements at OpenAI, Google, Together AI and NVIDIA, with one clear gain for buyers: Stability AI made Stable Audio generations much cheaper in credits.
points: OpenAI ended API access to a long list of older GPT and o-series models, naming GPT-5.6 models as replacements
Socket.dev’s Free plan now covers a single active developer after advertising unlimited developers and repos
HiveMQ stopped new Serverless clusters and will delete remaining ones at year end
Chroma Cloud is winding down as Chroma joins Replit, so data must be exported before it stops serving reads

news.title: 10 Lessons on AI Credits from Gong, Miro, and Databricks
news.gist: A roundtable with pricing leads from Gong, Miro and Databricks concludes that credits can be complex inside the vendor but must stay simple for customers: one pool, a familiar unit, metering on work done and controls from day one.
points: Gong ties a credit roughly to one analyzed call, so new features map back to a unit customers already understand
Panelists all preferred a single fungible pool, since separate pools strand credits and start rollover disputes
Start credit costs conservatively and lower them over time so changes land in the customer’s favor
Not everything should burn credits: Gong kept its AI role-play trainer unmetered after beta feedback
nums: changes in the issue’s weekly roundup
30 minutes
daily operations meeting Gong still holds months after its credits launch
Atlassian Statuspage’s new Business plan price per month, down from $399
news.why: When a vendor moves you onto credits, ask whether there is one pool, what a credit roughly equals and which spending caps you can set, since those decide how predictable the bill is.

patterns.p: AI and compute tools kept their list prices but cut how much a plan’s credits, minutes or hardware buy, a rise that never shows on the price line. All six come from PricingSaaS reports.

patterns.t: Cheapest plans removed, entry price climbs
patterns.p: Several vendors dropped their lowest paid or free tier, so the cheapest way in now costs more or goes through sales. Intercom’s list-price rise is softened by a new-customer discount. All six come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: Changes that cost buyers more outnumbered savings almost two to one
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that cost buyers more vs less; the other 31 repackage
stats_analysis.p: Straight list-price increases ran at twice the rate of cuts, 22 against 11, led by LaunchNotes’ Growth plan, RevenueHero’s platform fee and OneUp’s Enterprise floor. The deepest cuts were token and plan prices at Baseten, Highlight AI and Synthesia. Almost all of these records come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: Limits tightened far more often than they loosened
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that tighten vs loosen a limit
stats_analysis.p: Tightening ranged from HubSpot’s free email sends and Vercel’s firewall rules to new caps where none existed, such as SketchUp’s 3D Warehouse downloads and Grain’s meeting length. Loosening was rarer and smaller, like Zoom Basic’s in-meeting questions and Fleetio’s automation limits. Most tightened limits come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: AI was in about a third of the week
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that touch AI features or AI pricing
stats_analysis.p: Per-unit inference got cheaper at Baseten, Hive, fal and Leap AI, while app-level AI plans gave less for the same money at Pictory and Picsart. Unbounce put a meter on AI that was previously unlisted. Most of these come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: Free plans were reworked in both directions
stats_analysis.p: HubSpot, Jam, Seedance and Leonardo.ai gave free users less, and Kurrent turned its hosted free workspace into a local-only edition. Zoom, Koala and Tatsoft went the other way with bigger allowances, a new free plan and free production use. Apart from Zoom, these come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: The most relevant changes lean toward higher costs
stats_analysis.p: Five of the eleven raise costs, among them Intercom’s Essential seat, HubSpot’s free email sends and Zoom Rooms’ camera cap, while three cut prices or loosen limits and three repackage. Intercom’s WhatsApp unit, Zoom Basic’s allowance and Synthesia’s cut are our own captures; the rest come from PricingSaaS reports.

news_trends.t: Credits are now the default meter, and their design is the argument
news_trends.p: Good Better Best has spent weeks on how credits should work, from rollover and bonus rules to Notion’s split wallets and the Gong, Miro and Databricks case for one simple pool. HubSpot moving Starter email onto shared Credits and Arcade swapping seats for credit tiers show the shift reaching mainstream software, most of it seen through PricingSaaS reports.

This week Baseten cut a model’s launch rates within four days and Pulse flagged fal’s video cut and Krea’s flip-flop as likely tests, while fileAI reversed its own cut from the week before.
